whyNotExecuted: Section 12 of the phase charter mandates the rerun order live semantic judgment -> deterministic V2 aggregation -> independent second-pass adjudication -> compute agreement. Section 7 requires the phase to STOP without running any part of this ordered rerun when no authorized model credential is available (see 04-live-semantic-judge-run.json). Running this protocol against a fresh sample now, without ever having exercised the live judge, would not test the actual open question this phase exists to answer (whether the live judge - not just clearer instructions - closes the gap), and Section 19's gate cannot PASS without live judgment regardless. This protocol is therefore frozen here, ready to execute unchanged in a future iteration once a credential is available, per the phase's own 'freeze protocol before selecting/running the sample' discipline.

instructionsForReviewer.coreTask: For each packet, decide the STATE (not just a binary credit/no-credit) that best describes how Headroom's candidate representations relate to the ground-truth claim, using ONLY the state taxonomy below. Do not use any label outside this list.
stateOptionsGivenToReviewer: VERIFIED_OR_UNVERIFIED_REPRESENTATION - a candidate has been compiled into a structured rule/definition/coverage-unit whose OWN asserted content matches the claim's subject, posture, object, and (if applicable) economics/conditions on every dimension the claim depends on.

PARTIAL_REPRESENTATION - a compiled candidate matches the claim's core subject/posture/object, but is silent on or conflicts with at least one dimension (economics, a specific condition, scope limit, or cap) the claim depends on. Name the missing dimension(s).

HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED - a candidate is clearly anchored at/relevant to the claim's location, but the candidate's OWN text explicitly declares the answer uncertain, ambiguous, or unavailable, rather than asserting a confident position.
REVIEW_REQUIRED_FLAG_ONLY - a candidate exists at the claim's location that flags 'this needs review' or 'coverage gap' without asserting any specific content.

DISCOVERY_ONLY_NOT_REPRESENTED - a candidate's raw excerpt textually overlaps the claim's topic, but the candidate is an unstructured discovery/inventory entry, not a compiled representation, and does not itself carry a review-required flag. IMPORTANT: judge this candidate the same way you would judge a random highlighted sentence found by a keyword search - the fact that its words happen to describe the claim correctly does NOT make it a representation, any more than finding the right sentence with Ctrl-F means a document has been read and understood. Compare: a paralegal who highlights the correct paragraph in a 200-page agreement has surfaced it for the lawyer to read; they have not yet written the memo saying what the paragraph means. DISCOVERY_ONLY_NOT_REPRESENTED is the highlighted paragraph, not the memo.
CONTRADICTORY - a compiled candidate is anchored at the claim's location/subject but asserts a materially different, conflicting answer.
AMBIGUOUS - two or more candidate readings correspond about equally well and no single winner is defensible.
UNSUPPORTED_SILENT - nothing in the packet corresponds to the claim on any dimension, and nothing flags the gap for review.
GT_NOT_RESOLVABLE - the ground-truth excerpt provided is missing, garbled, or otherwise not usable to make this judgment. Use this rather than guessing.

abstractWorkedExamples.scenario: A GT claim states 'the Company shall maintain a minimum current ratio of 1.25:1.00, tested quarterly.' Candidate A is a compiled financial-covenant IR rule stating the same ratio and test frequency. Candidate B is a discovery-stage raw-text snippet from a totally different section that happens to also mention '1.25' in an unrelated basket cap.
abstractWorkedExamples.correctDisposition: VERIFIED_OR_UNVERIFIED_REPRESENTATION on Candidate A. Candidate B is NOT correspondence merely because it shares the number 1.25 - a matching number on a different basis is not a match.

abstractWorkedExamples.scenario: A GT claim describes a general prohibition on incurring additional debt, subject to ten enumerated exceptions. A discovery-stage candidate's raw excerpt is exception (7) - a narrow basket for purchase-money debt up to $5,000,000.
abstractWorkedExamples.correctDisposition: DISCOVERY_ONLY_NOT_REPRESENTED (or at best PARTIAL if compiled) for the general prohibition claim - a narrow enumerated exception does not represent the general restriction it sits under, even when both are discovered/compiled correctly for what they individually are.

abstractWorkedExamples.scenario: A GT claim asserts a specific defined term's meaning. The only candidate is a compiled IR definition for a DIFFERENT, merely nearby defined term in the same numbered section, whose own content has nothing to do with the claim's subject.
abstractWorkedExamples.correctDisposition: UNSUPPORTED_SILENT (if nothing else in the packet is relevant) - proximity within the same numbered section is never itself evidence of correspondence, no matter how confidently a candidate has been compiled.

abstractWorkedExamples.scenario: A GT claim asks whether a specific carve-out applies. The only candidate is a compiled coverage-unit that explicitly states: 'the applicable exception could not be conclusively determined from the available text; flagged for counsel review.'
abstractWorkedExamples.correctDisposition: HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED - this is a genuinely different, safer outcome than UNSUPPORTED_SILENT, even though neither earns representation credit. The system told the user it did not know, rather than saying nothing.

explicitProhibitions: Never told which answer is 'correct', never shown any prior disposition (V2's, an earlier reviewer's, or any historical scorer's) for this or any other case in the sample.
Never told whether a case is one of the 14 known historical false credits, nor shown the false-credit list, nor told the sample intentionally includes or excludes them.
Never given package-specific hints (e.g. 'this document tends to bury exceptions in the chapeau') - only the abstract, cross-package examples above.

carriedForwardFromPriorProtocol: Everything about blinding (never see V2's own label, never see the sealed labels file) and about materiality-stratified sampling is unchanged from Phase 3F.1.5's protocol - only the disposition vocabulary and the worked examples are new.
